 THE HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SYAM KUMAR V.M.
 Friday, the 7th day of February 2025 / 18th Magha, 1946  CM.APPL.NO.1/2025 IN WA NO. 248 OF 2025  AGAINST JUDGMENT DATED 08/01/2020 IN WP(C) 17303/2019 OF THIS COURT APPLICANTS/APPELLANT:
 K.J.FRANCIS, AGED 82 YEARS, S/O LATE RAPHEL JOSEPH, KONNOTH HOUSE,
 RAMESWARAM VILLAGE, ERNAKULAM DISTRICT, NOW RESIDING AT KONNOTH  HOUSE, KEZHUTHUMUKKU, THOPUMPADI, KOCHI - 682005 RESPONDENTS/RESPONDENTS  1. STATE OF KERALA, REPRESENTED BY ITS SECRETARY, REVENUE DEPARTMENT,

Application praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed therewith the High Court be pleased to condone the delay of 1125 (one thousand one hundred and twenty-five days) days in filing the above appeal.

This Application coming on for orders on 07/02/2025 upon perusing the application and the affidavit filed in support thereof, and upon hearing the arguments of ADVS.M/S.VARGHESE K.PAUL, KASHMEERA ASHRAF,
SMT.SNEHA DIVAKARAN P., ANAMIKA SASIKUMAR, SAFEER BAWA A.S for the applicant, and of SENIOR GOVERNMENT PLEADER K.P.HARISH FOR R1 & R2

, the court on the same day passed the following:
 NITIN JAMDAR, C.J.
 &
 SYAM KUMAR V.M, J.
 =========================
 C.M. Application No.1/2025 in  W.A. No. 248 of 2025  =========================
 Dated this the 7th day of February 2025  ORDER Heard Mr. Safeer Bawa A.S. representing Mr. Varghese K. Paul, learned counsel for the Appellant and Mr. K.P. Harish, learned Senior Government Pleader for the State.
2.
The delay in filing the appeal is of 1125 days.
The appeal is filed challenging the order passed by the learned Single Judge dated 8 January 2020 partly allowing the petition.
As far as the part which is against the State, the State has filed W.A.No.1262/2020, which was filed with delay of 219 days.

The delay was condoned on 9 October 2020 and the appeal was admitted on 4 February 2025.

4. In the application for condonation of delay in the present appeal, the Applicant has stated as under:
"3. I am a senior citizen and I reside with my wife, also a senior citizen, and my youngest son who is deaf and mute, assessed as having 80% disability.
My eldest son has deserted the family and has not been involved in supporting the family since the year 2012.
A great deal of our savings and property was expended in his education as also in funding his migration abroad.
As a result, we are constantly under a great deal of physical and mental duress to make ends meet.
I am forced to work several hours every day in harsh conditions for meagre wages for survival.

4. When the land belonging to our father was illegally taken over by the Corporation,
the last hope of substantial income for the sustenance of my family was lost.
It was after filing several consecutive representations before various authorities without any redressal that I approached this Hon'ble Court by filing a writ petition.

Being socially and economically backward in addition to being significantly limited in physical ability, as a consequence of my advanced age, I did not have at my disposal the necessary knowledge or social connections to approach this Hon'ble Court seeking appropriate relief against the arbitrary state action.

Like many people in my position,
I too believed that approaching the High Court is a costly affair, which I could not readily afford.

It was after several months of deliberation with my siblings and concerted efforts to accumulate funds to afford a competent lawyer that I was finally able to approach this Hon'ble Court by filing a writ petition.

5. It was informed to me by my Advocate on 08-01- 2020 itself that my petition was disposed directing the 3rd respondent to deposit with the Collector, the amount as per the Tahsildar's valuation of our property and the same shall be released to us after executing a sale deed in respect of the subject property in favour of the 3rd respondent.
No amounts were deposited thereafter in compliance with the judgment and hence, no sale deed was executed either.

In consideration of the submissions of my Advocate on my behalf, the learned Single Judge had recorded the fact that the value ascertained by the Tahsildar is under dispute and hence, a reference ought to be made under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The same was also not carried out since no amount was deposited with the Collector.

As a consequence, I was left with no means at the time to re-agitate this issue before this Hon'ble Court by filing a contempt petition, for I had already exhausted what little funds that 1 had while filing the appeal.
6. The financial distress faced by me has been compounded by the plethora of illnesses that I am afflicted with Consequently, I am no longer in a position to fend for myself or support my family.

To any extent, I am no longer an able-bodied person K.J.Francis vs State Of Kerala on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45452181/
2 and require assistance in my day-to-day life

I was admitted to the General Hospital,
Ernakulam on multiple occasions during the year, 2024, with severe and recurrent infections m the urinary tract.
During the course of medical examination, it has been found that my kidneys are also showing signs of distress and deterioration
Accordingly, I have now been prescribed with medications to preserve my kidney functions.
A consequence of the combination of my ailments is that I am presently unable to exert myself physically or engage in productive labour.
I have therefore been relegated to tending to the household as my wife too is severely ill.

7. Due to severe financial distress and my inability to better my family's situation, I was constrained to file a petition under Section 125 of the Criminal Procedure Code against my eldest son, seeking maintenance.

As stated above, both my wife and I are physically incapable of taking care of ourselves and meeting our day-to-day needs,
including medical treatments.
My younger son, being disabled, is also unable to adequately fend for himself, let alone support the family.
In fact, he requires constant care and support due to his condition.
The petition for maintenance is presently pending before the Hon'ble Family Court Ernakulam as M.C. No. 30/2024.
It was due to the unfortunate confluence of excruciating circumstances as delineated above that I was unable to appeal against the order of the learned Single Judge within the stipulated time.
8. Moreover, my wife is also severely ailing and require substantial expenditure towards here medicines and treatments.
She suffers from severe case of diabetes and have had to undergo surgeries on her limbs as a result.
Her blood sugar levels require constant monitoring in order to prevent lows and resultant comatose.
Due to her age and weakened immunity, coupled with diabetes, her body is riddled with a variety of illnesses and hence require constant medical attention and periodic checkups for early detection.
My younger son is the sole breadwinner and is burdened with the responsibility of taking care of his aged and ailing parents.
His income is not sufficient for the family's daily meals, let alone legal pursuit."

4. Considering the above cause and that the appeal filed by the State against the same impugned judgment is already admitted, we are of the opinion that the cause is made out for condonation of delay in filing the appeal by the Appellant / Original Petitioner.
Delay is condoned.
Application is allowed.
5. Admit.
To be heard along with W.A.No.1262/2020.

Sd/-
